# A submenu is a sibling of its menu for focus, not its child

## Context

Follow-up to #18847 / PR #18860, from a second look @tobiu asked for through the `manager.Focus` model. Same seam as #18838 the same day, where a picker field's floating picker carried no `parentComponent` and a 43-line grid-plugin workaround collapsed into one line of ownership (PR #18852).

handoff: @neo-opus-grace — `menu.List` focus is your surface today (#18846–#18848, #18860). Decline freely; then it is claimable.

## The Problem

`menu.List#showSubMenu()` creates every level with `parentComponent: me.parentComponent` and `parentId: app.mainView.id`: all levels are siblings under the ROOT's owner. `manager.Focus` works on `ComponentManager.getParentPath` — the first component in the DOM path, then `component.parent` — so a focus move between a level and its submenu shares no menu. The level losing focus gets `focusLeave`, `component.Base#onFocusLeave` clears its `focusEnterData`, and `containsFocus` answers for one level only.

`menu.List` answers that with bookkeeping of its own: `menuFocus_` bubbling up `parentMenu`, the `oldPath` scans in `onFocusLeave` (`leftPathIsOwnTree`, `isInteractionPath(data.oldPath)`), and — with PR #18860 — `focusSource` and the `holdsFocus()` recursion. Each is correct; together they restate what the component tree answers when a submenu is owned by the level that opened it.

## The Architectural Reality

Measured on PR #18860's head (`8338bf1d57`), component tier `menu` + `button`, 45 arms:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `parentComponent: me` in `showSubMenu()`, nothing else | 43 green · 2 red: `a rest pending from arrowing onto a parent does not reopen what Right and Left closed`, `Space on a parent enters its submenu, and Space on a leaf dismisses like Enter` |
| + `holdsFocus()` reduced to `containsFocus`, the `focusSource` hand-back in `unmount()` switched off | the same 2 red; all 8 arms PR #18860 adds stay green — the inherited `revertFocus()` returns focus to the trigger, because the root never left focus |
| + `onFocusMove` rests only when `path` AND `oldPath` are inside this level | 44 green · 1 red: `Space on a parent…` — undiagnosed; hypothesis: the keydown now reaches ancestor levels through `manager.DomEvent#verifyDelegationPath` phase 2 (logical ancestry) |

- `onFocusMove`'s JSDoc relies on the sibling shape ("`ArrowRight` moving focus INTO a submenu shares an ancestor of both menus instead, and never reaches this method"). Under ownership it does reach it, in both directions.
- `hideSubMenu()`'s explicit hand-back to the opening item stays either way: `revertFocus()` focuses `Neo.getComponent(relatedTarget.id)`, and an item is a node, not a component.
- Precedent for owning a floating part: `button.Base` (its menu), `tab/plugin/Overflow`, `grid/column/Component`, and `form.field.Picker` since PR #18852.

## The Fix

`showSubMenu()` creates a submenu with `parentComponent: me`. Then delete what the tree now answers: `focusSource`, `holdsFocus()`, and — measure first — the `menuFocus` bubbling and the `oldPath` scans in `onFocusLeave`. `onFocusMove` distinguishes an item-to-item move from a move between a level and its submenu; key events handled by a level do not act again in its ancestors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every arm of `component/menu` and `component/button` stays green, PR #18860's 8 hand-back arms included.
- [ ] `focusSource` and `holdsFocus()` are gone; a full dismissal returns focus through the inherited `revertFocus()`.
- [ ] Each remaining piece of menu-local focus bookkeeping (`menuFocus_` bubbling, the `onFocusLeave` scans) is either deleted or kept with the measurement that says why.
- [ ] Net engine lines in `src/menu/List.mjs` go down; the PR names the number.

## Out of Scope

Pointer dismissal (`isInteractionPath` for `onAppMouseDown`) · `menu.Panel` · teaching `revertFocus()` to focus a node that is not a component.

## Avoided Traps

- **Folding it into PR #18860:** that PR fixes what users hit today and its arms are the net this change needs; it should not wait.
- **Reading the numbers above as done:** they are one afternoon's experiment on a detached head, three edits, no review. The Space path is open.
